setup: Stand side-on, a step away from the stack
Handle in the near hand, arm long
execution: Bend sideways away from the cable
Lean back toward the cable for a stretch
Finish one side, then turn round
faults: Don't go heavy and jerk the handle

notes: Use a moderate weight and a range you can control; there is no need to bend to the extreme each way.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Side plank
regressions.reason: Hold the trunk still against gravity before loading a bend.

progressions.name: Cable side bend with a pause
progressions.reason: A short hold at the top adds difficulty without more weight.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell side bend
substitutions.reason: Same movement with a dumbbell; load is that dumbbell.

substitutions.name: Farmer's carry
substitutions.reason: The obliques resist leaning while you walk.

substitutions.name: Cable woodchop
substitutions.reason: Obliques on the same cable column, with rotation.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at waist height, figure facing the camera with the cable column to one side. The cable line from the low pulley to the hand stays visible.

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall side-on to the column, feet hip width. Near arm long holding the handle at the side of the thigh. Trunk bent a little toward the cable.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Trunk bent sideways away from the cable, near arm still long, handle risen up the outside of the thigh. Chest still facing forward, hips level over the feet.

ikHints: Hand fixed to the handle; cable runs straight to the low pulley
emphasise: Pure side bend; chest stays facing forward
Working side is the side away from the cable
doNotShow: Bending far past a comfortable range
